_comment: Source of truth for crash-dump configuration. The configure step (configure-dumps.ps1) applies these registry values under CrashControl so a dump is actually written when a BSOD occurs; the collector verifies the live settings match before trusting that a dump would have been produced. 'crashDumpType' values follow the CrashDumpEnabled registry semantics.
_source: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl. See Microsoft docs: 'Overview of memory dump file options for Windows'.

complete.description: Complete memory dump: entire physical memory. Requires page file >= RAM size (+1MB) or a dedicated dump file.

kernel.description: Kernel memory dump: kernel-mode read/write pages only. Good default for driver crashes.

small.description: Small (mini) dump, 64KB-ish, written to %SystemRoot%\Minidump. Minimum useful dump.

automatic.description: Automatic memory dump (Win8+): like kernel dump but lets the OS manage page-file sizing.

filtered.description: Variable size. Filters out VM host/guest memory overhead, making offline extraction faster than full complete dumps on high-RAM servers.

recommended.notes: CrashDumpEnabled=7 (Automatic). DedicatedDumpFile intentionally absent — it forces StorPort crash miniport which fails on VirtIO/SCSI (issue #1629). pagefile.sys (RAM+257MB) used for Phase 1 crash dump staging via normal I/O. AutoReboot=0 keeps VM frozen for offline extraction.

pageFile.notes: pagefile.sys sized at RAM+257MB. Used for crash dump Phase 1 staging via normal I/O (not crash miniport). 257MB buffer prevents Windows from deallocating pagefile on high-free-RAM KVM systems.
